title: Black & White Taxicab & Transfer Co. v. Brown & Yellow Taxicab & Transfer Co. (1928)
summary: The case illustrated how the Swift regime permitted strategic incorporation to obtain a different substantive rule in federal court.
notes:
The syllabus calls this “Black & White Taxicab.” The record is a historical comparison within Erie’s reasoning, not a current rule governing exclusive station arrangements.

Justice Holmes dissented, joined by Justices Brandeis and Stone, arguing that the common law enforced in a state is the law of that state existing by its authority and that the Swift doctrine was an unconstitutional assumption of power by the federal courts; the majority (Butler, J., 6-3) upheld the exclusive contract with the Louisville & Nashville Railroad for the Bowling Green, Kentucky station after the Kentucky owners reincorporated in Tennessee and dissolved the Kentucky company.

sections.Parties: Competing taxicab companies disputed an exclusive arrangement involving access to a railroad station.
sections.Material Facts: The relevant business and agreement were centered in Kentucky, whose law disfavored the exclusive arrangement. A company reorganized under Tennessee law, creating diverse citizenship and access to federal court. The federal general-law approach then permitted a result different from the rule the Kentucky courts would apply.
sections.Procedural History: The Supreme Court allowed the federal general-law treatment under Swift. Erie later identified the case as an example of the regime’s problematic consequences.
sections.Issue: Could the strategically obtained federal forum apply its own general law to the arrangement despite contrary state doctrine?
sections.Holding: Under the pre-Erie regime, it could. Erie rejected the broader legal framework that made that result possible.
sections.Reasoning: The episode demonstrates that forum choice could change substantive rights instead of merely changing the tribunal. Corporate reorganization made the alternative law available to one side even though the underlying transaction remained local. Erie’s critique focused on that disparity and the incentives it created.

learning.why: The case illustrated how the Swift regime permitted strategic incorporation to obtain a different substantive rule in federal court.

topics.cp-forum-shopping: Changing corporate citizenship enabled access to a federal general-law rule unavailable in state court.
topics.cp-erie-history: Erie used this episode to illustrate the inequities of Swift.
topics.cp-citizenship: The reincorporation in Tennessee manufactured diverse corporate citizenship to reach federal court.
topics.cp-diversity: The case shows diversity jurisdiction being used to obtain a different substantive rule under Swift.
topics.cp-erie: Erie cited the case as the example of Swift's abuses and Holmes's dissent supplied Erie's constitutional reasoning.

mnemonic.rationale: A taxi company reincorporated to shop for law
